name: Multidirectional Instability of the Shoulder
definition: Symptomatic instability of the glenohumeral joint in more than one direction, often related to capsular laxity and impaired dynamic stabilization.

investigations.principle: Imaging is selective; diagnosis is primarily clinical with MRI used to evaluate structural lesions when needed.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, ligament, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

green: Structured scapular and rotator-cuff stabilization rehabilitation
amber: Surgery is reserved for persistent disabling instability after high-quality rehabilitation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-Sandhi asthirata phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Symptomatic instability of the glenohumeral joint in more than one direction, often related to capsular laxity and impaired dynamic stabilization.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected serious infection, airway/vascular symptoms, unreduced dislocation or other listed red flags.
